publishedWalks.title: The Highgate Village Self-Guided Walk — Richard Jones
stops: Advertised route includes Highgate station, North Road, Highgate School, Gatehouse, Pond Square, Church House, Highgate Literary and Scientific Institute, St Michael’s, Flask, reservoir, The Grove, Holly Lodge, Holly Village, cemetery entrances, Waterlow Park and Whittington Stone; finishes at Archway. Locator: lines 51–200. ([london-walking-tours.co.uk](https://www.london-walking-tours.co.uk/free-tours/highgate-village-walk.htm))
themes: Dickens, literary associations, pubs, philanthropy and village history; advertised as two hours, not a station-return loop. ([london-walking-tours.co.uk](https://www.london-walking-tours.co.uk/free-tours/highgate-village-walk.htm))
stories: North Road family lodging and creditors; pub initiation customs; suggested David Copperfield settings; Coleridge and Gillman. These are the guide’s claims, not independently verified evidence. Origin: commercial walking-tour publisher; publication date not established. ([london-walking-tours.co.uk](https://www.london-walking-tours.co.uk/free-tours/highgate-village-walk.htm))

publishedWalks.title: Highgate Village: Tales of History and Mystery — Deborah Greenfield / Highgate Society
stops: Western cemetery entrance → Waterlow Park → Lauderdale House → High Street → Pond Square. These are explicitly advertised places, not a complete stop inventory. Locator: lines 73–83. ([highgatesociety.com](https://highgatesociety.com/highgate-village-tales-of-history-and-mystery/))
themes: Village architecture, environment, famous residents, philanthropy, ghosts and pub traditions; advertised duration 60 minutes. ([highgatesociety.com](https://highgatesociety.com/highgate-village-tales-of-history-and-mystery/))
stories: Advertises resistance to road widening, Swearing on the Horns, Graham Chapman’s writing, Romantic poets and Dickens settings. The Nell Gwyn window episode is advertised but not established here as historical fact. Origin: local civic society promoting a commercial audio tour; page dated August 22, 2025; locator: lines 72–90. Audio not purchased or heard. ([highgatesociety.com](https://highgatesociety.com/highgate-village-tales-of-history-and-mystery/))

publishedWalks.title: Highgate Walks — A Local History Guide — Joan Schwitzer
stops: Walk 1: Highgate Hill and Highgate High Street.
Walk 2: Pond Square and The Grove.
Walk 3: Southwood Lane and North Road.

Walk 4: Highgate Cemetery and Waterlow Park. These are advertised coverage areas; individual stops are not available on the sales page. ([hornseyhistorical.org.uk](https://hornseyhistorical.org.uk/highgate-walks-local-history-guide/))
themes: Historic sites and the origins and histories of buildings. Origin: Hornsey Historical Society; first published 1989, advertised edition revised 2016. Locator: lines 48–60. ([hornseyhistorical.org.uk](https://hornseyhistorical.org.uk/highgate-walks-local-history-guide/))
stories: No individual anecdotes exposed in the opened listing. Book neither purchased nor read; do not treat its advertised scope as consulted historical evidence. ([hornseyhistorical.org.uk](https://hornseyhistorical.org.uk/highgate-walks-local-history-guide/))

publishedWalks.title: Waterlow Park illustrated trail guide — Friends of Waterlow Park
stops: Fourteen numbered features include Lauderdale House, statues, terraces, eagle steps, kitchen garden and orchard, hollow oak, middle pond, playground, Swain’s Lane Lodge, lion gates, lime avenue, upper pond, tennis courts and London viewpoint. Locator: PDF page 1, items 1–14. ([waterlowpark.org.uk](https://www.waterlowpark.org.uk/media/publications/Waterlow_guide.pdf))
themes: Historic gardens, public recreation, horticulture, wildlife and philanthropy. Origin: park friends group; publication date not established. ([waterlowpark.org.uk](https://www.waterlowpark.org.uk/media/publications/Waterlow_guide.pdf))
stories: Advertises Pepys’s 1666 visit, conversion of Waterlow’s estate into a public park, traces of a carriage drive and community growing. Nell Gwyn’s stay, the oak’s age, lion-gate dating and an underground shelter are qualified rather than certain. ([waterlowpark.org.uk](https://www.waterlowpark.org.uk/media/publications/Waterlow_guide.pdf))

publishedWalks.title: Historic walk in Highgate Wood — Michael Hammerson / City of London
stops: Information Hut beside the café is the advertised start. Further numbered stops remain unknown because the linked leaflet failed to load. ([cityoflondon.gov.uk](https://www.cityoflondon.gov.uk/things-to-do/green-spaces/highgate-wood/historic-walk-in-highgate-wood))
themes: Self-guided woodland history; approximately two hours. Origin: land-manager website; updated October 29, 2024; locator: lines 23–31. ([cityoflondon.gov.uk](https://www.cityoflondon.gov.uk/things-to-do/green-spaces/highgate-wood/historic-walk-in-highgate-wood))
stories: No specific stories exposed in the landing page. This is a partially catalogued guide, not evidence for particular woodland anecdotes. ([cityoflondon.gov.uk](https://www.cityoflondon.gov.uk/things-to-do/green-spaces/highgate-wood/historic-walk-in-highgate-wood))

candidates.name: North Road — Dickens lodging lead
candidates.why: Proposal: domestic financial insecurity rather than celebrity alone. Guide locates lodging near the former Red Lion, lines 58–64. Exact frontage and public standing point unresolved. ([london-walking-tours.co.uk](https://www.london-walking-tours.co.uk/free-tours/highgate-village-walk.htm))

candidates.name: Highgate Literary and Scientific Institute exterior
candidates.why: Proposal: neighbourhood learning and voluntary institutions. Guide identifies 11 South Grove and an 1839 foundation, lines 93–97. Pavement viewpoint proposed; archive access unnecessary. ([london-walking-tours.co.uk](https://www.london-walking-tours.co.uk/free-tours/highgate-village-walk.htm))

candidates.name: Reservoir mound near The Grove
candidates.why: Proposal: hidden infrastructure explaining village life. Guide associates the mound with piped water in 1854, line 118. Public-path sightline needs verification. ([london-walking-tours.co.uk](https://www.london-walking-tours.co.uk/free-tours/highgate-village-walk.htm))

candidates.name: High Street — conservation and road-widening conflict
candidates.why: Proposal: invite newcomers to understand the streetscape as something contested rather than inevitable. The Society advertises a 1962 demolition threat and residents’ resistance, lines 72–79. Verify the scheme, chronology and affected buildings before choosing a specific public pavement anchor. ([highgatesociety.com](https://highgatesociety.com/highgate-village-tales-of-history-and-mystery/))

candidates.name: Pond Square — ritual and belonging
candidates.why: Proposal: examine who became an honorary local through pub ritual. The Society locates its concluding Swearing on the Horns story here, line 75; this does not establish that the ceremony happened in the square. Proposed anchor: public square, precise standing point unresolved. ([highgatesociety.com](https://highgatesociety.com/highgate-village-tales-of-history-and-mystery/))

candidates.name: Lauderdale House and terraces
candidates.why: Proposal: contrast documented visiting with royal legend, anchored outside the house. Trail items 1–3 date the house approximately and distinguish a recorded Pepys visit from a reported Nell Gwyn stay. Check primary evidence; no interior entry required. ([waterlowpark.org.uk](https://www.waterlowpark.org.uk/media/publications/Waterlow_guide.pdf))

candidates.name: Waterlow Park — London viewpoint
candidates.why: Proposal: connect a visible city outlook with private wealth becoming public recreation. Trail item 14 and its closing paragraph link Waterlow, his printing business and the park’s opening. Exact bench, sightline and gate access unresolved. ([waterlowpark.org.uk](https://www.waterlowpark.org.uk/media/publications/Waterlow_guide.pdf))

candidates.name: Waterlow Park kitchen garden and orchard
candidates.why: Proposal: living community activity rather than another famous resident. Trail item 5 identifies communal growing spaces below the park centre. Observe from a public path only; current planting and entry arrangements unverified. ([waterlowpark.org.uk](https://www.waterlowpark.org.uk/media/publications/Waterlow_guide.pdf))

candidates.name: Highgate Cemetery western entrance exterior
candidates.why: Proposal: architecture and the boundary between public street and burial ground, without admission. The Society explicitly starts outside its neo-Gothic western entrance, line 73. A specific non-obstructing public standing point and exterior-only story remain to be researched. ([highgatesociety.com](https://highgatesociety.com/highgate-village-tales-of-history-and-mystery/))

candidates.name: Highgate Wood Information Hut — alternative woodland branch
candidates.why: Proposal: diversify selection beyond village celebrities and gardens. The official historic walk starts here, but its detailed stories remain unavailable. Treat as an alternative branch, not an addition to an assumed one-hour village loop; route and evidence blockers unresolved. ([cityoflondon.gov.uk](https://www.cityoflondon.gov.uk/things-to-do/green-spaces/highgate-wood/historic-walk-in-highgate-wood))
